per_depth.shortcut_name: Steiner-tree recognition via optional relay sites
per_depth.common_affordance: The non-required sites may be used as intermediate relay vertices while only the required sites must be connected.
The solution may use arbitrary non-required sites as Steiner intermediates while only required sites must be mutually connected.
The at-most-ten priority-terminal Steiner-tree structure, which makes a 2^t subset DP feasible
A small explicitly bounded terminal set allows exponential subset DP for the Steiner tree, while all hubs remain available as shared relays.
The problem is a weighted Steiner-tree/connectivity problem with at most 10 terminals, making exponential-in-t subset DP feasible.
The activated rules form an undirected connected subgraph containing all targets, with arbitrary non-target variables allowed as Steiner relay vertices.
The task is exactly finding a minimum-cost connected subgraph containing all target vertices, with arbitrary non-target intermediate vertices allowed.
The problem is exactly a weighted Steiner-tree problem on the graph of available transpositions, with at most ten designated terminals.

The equality mandates are transitive, so the selected mandate edges only need to form a connected subgraph containing all centerpiece canvases; arbitrary non-centerpiece canvases may serve as Steiner vertices.
The terminal set has at most ten vertices, making exponential-in-t subset DP practical.
